content.user_title: Plan SMS and WhatsApp Marketing Campaigns
content.value_statement: Messaging campaigns need clear consent, relevant timing, and careful cost control. This skill helps draft sequences, compare platforms, and define compliance checks and performance measures.
actual_capabilities: Design welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase, replenishment, and win-back flows with triggers, delays, segmentation, and exit conditions.
Draft concise SMS copy with sender identification, calls to action, character counts, and opt-out language.
Outline consent, registration, quiet-hour, and STOP/HELP checks for messaging programs across major jurisdictions.
Compare SMS providers using business type, existing tools, list size, integration needs, and approximate costs.
Plan WhatsApp template categories, customer service windows, opt-in handling, and support handoffs.
Propose campaign KPIs, attribution tags, and A/B tests for timing, offers, personalization, and message format.
limitations: Provides planning guidance and templates, not a standalone message sender or deployed automation.
Does not replace legal advice or guarantee compliance with current laws and carrier requirements.
Platform pricing, WhatsApp policies, and benchmark figures require independent verification before use.
Live integrations, account registration, template approval, and performance data require external platforms and authorized access.

use_cases.title: Recover abandoned carts
use_cases.description: Create a consent-based cart reminder sequence with purchase exits, delayed discounts, and coordinated email timing.

use_cases.title: Plan transactional notifications
use_cases.description: Compare messaging providers and outline order alerts, consent boundaries, registration needs, and STOP/HELP handling.

use_cases.title: Design international WhatsApp flows
use_cases.description: Draft approved-template plans, marketing opt-ins, service-window rules, and human support handoffs for international audiences.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a welcome message
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a welcome SMS for [brand] with [offer], [short link], sender identification, and STOP/HELP instructions. State the character count and encoding assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: write the first message after a documented marketing opt-in.

prompt_templates.title: Design a cart recovery flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an SMS cart recovery flow for [store] in [country] using [platform]. Include consent checks, timing, copy, purchase exits, quiet hours, and delayed discounts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: plan an automation before configuring it in a messaging platform.

prompt_templates.title: Compare platforms and costs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare SMS platforms for [business] with [stack], [subscriber count], and [monthly sends]. Explain registration responsibilities, cost assumptions, integration needs, and facts requiring verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a provider shortlist and implementation checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a multichannel program
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan SMS and WhatsApp flows for [business] across [countries]. Separate marketing and transactional consent, template categories, service windows, suppression rules, costs, KPIs, and experiments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate international messaging with compliance checks and measurement.

output_examples.input: Plan cart recovery for a US Shopify store using Klaviyo with documented marketing consent.
output: Before launch: confirm registration for the selected sender type, consent records, STOP/HELP handling, and recipient-local quiet hours.
First reminder: send 30 minutes after abandonment during allowed hours, without a discount.
Draft: From Acme: Your cart is waiting: [cart link]. Reply STOP to opt out.
Follow-up: send only if no purchase occurs; reserve any discount for a later message.
Exit immediately on purchase or opt-out, and track conversions, cost per send, and unsubscribe rate.

output_examples.input: Outline a WhatsApp order-update and promotional program for opted-in customers in Brazil.
output: Keep order-update consent separate from promotional consent and record both in the customer profile.
Use utility templates for non-promotional order updates outside the customer service window.
Classify offers and cart reminders as marketing templates and provide a clear opt-out.
Route customer replies to support and verify the service-window expiry before using free-form messages.
Confirm current Meta and provider fees before estimating monthly costs.

best_practices: Verify documented consent, applicable registration, recipient-local quiet hours, and STOP/HELP responses before activating any campaign.
Recalculate character counts and segment costs after replacing placeholders and applying the actual message encoding.
Coordinate channels, stop sequences after purchases or opt-outs, and monitor conversion and unsubscribe rates.
anti_patterns: Sending marketing messages to purchased lists or contacts without valid consent.
Treating informational consent as permission for promotional offers or cross-selling.
Copying template urgency, prices, or policy claims without checking their accuracy and current applicability.

faq.question: Does this skill send messages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and drafts; sending requires a configured platform and authorized access.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it support WhatsApp as well as SMS?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers WhatsApp templates, opt-ins, customer service windows, quality limits, and support handoffs, alongside SMS and MMS planning.

faq.question: Does its checklist guarantee legal compliance?
faq.answer: No. Treat it as operational guidance and have qualified counsel review applicable laws, consent wording, and program settings.

faq.question: Are the listed prices and benchmarks current guarantees?
faq.answer: No. Confirm current vendor pricing, Meta policies, and carrier rules, then validate assumptions against your own campaign data.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide your business type, customer countries, platform, list size, consent process, registration status, existing flows, and campaign goal.
